memory_update.text: PLPC should be tracked as an underfollowed US-listed transmission-line hardware candidate adjacent to high-voltage grid buildout, but not yet as a confirmed HVDC reactor supplier.
AMSC maps more directly to grid power-quality and renewable-interconnection systems through Gridtec and D-VAR; verify whether grid revenue/backlog is material enough to survive later Serenity layers.

POWL is an adjacent electrical distribution and substation-control candidate with strong backlog evidence, but its historical oil/gas and petrochemical exposure must be separated from grid/electrification demand.

For US-listed equities, pure-play HVDC reactor exposure appears scarce; the more actionable US universe may be adjacent suppliers: transmission hardware, STATCOM/power quality, switchgear/control systems, and diversified T&D components.
Need primary-source verification for non-US pure-play suppliers such as Quality Power Electrical Equipments and then map any US-listed customers, suppliers, or competitors.

node: High-voltage reactors, HVDC components, grid power-quality systems, and renewable-integration equipment
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the high-voltage / HVDC-adjacent grid equipment node with a two-lane funnel. Reference context remains Hubbell as a diversified utility T&D component leader. The underfollowed lane is more interesting for Serenity Layer 1B: PLPC for transmission-line hardware, AMSC for grid power-quality / STATCOM / renewable-interconnection systems, and POWL for custom-engineered electrical distribution and substation-control exposure. None of these should be treated as confirmed HVDC-reactor pure plays; the working hypothesis is that long qualification cycles, utility/OEM approvals, and grid-equipment shortages may create backlog durability for niche suppliers adjacent to the high-voltage buildout.
